era help.name: ERA Help — guide and JSON examples

0.name: Open / close help
0.description: Open the help dialogue; F1 closes the main help window when it is already open.

1.description: Open the searchable result list from the main help window.

3.description: Close a result list, filter picker, object card or guide.

categories.name: Welcome
categories.content: Press F1 to open help. Browse the tabs or type in the Search field.

categories.name: Browsing objects
categories.content: Left click a portrait or name for details. Hold the right mouse button for a popup preview.

categories.name: Combining filters
categories.content: Categories are on the left; other filters are above the objects. Left click advances a filter; right click goes back. Reset clears filters and restores ID order.

categories.name: Selecting several levels
categories.content: Click level buttons to select several levels. Click again to remove a level.

categories.name: Creature filters
categories.content: Combine town, level, movement, attack, life and upgrade filters.

categories.name: Artifact filters
categories.content: Combine artifact class, position, availability, combination and spell filters.

categories.name: Hero filters
categories.content: Filter by town, class, availability, spellbook and gender.

categories.name: Spell filters
categories.content: Combine school, level, use, damage and mass-effect filters. Creature abilities include native IDs 70–80.

categories.name: Secondary skills
categories.content: All 28 skills fit at 800x600. Browse skill groups and compare Basic, Advanced and Expert effects.

categories.name: Town reference
categories.content: Town names, creature rosters and hero classes come from the game.

categories.name: Global search
categories.content: Type a title in the top Search field or press Ctrl+F to focus it. Results appear in this window. Choose a scope on the left. Article text and descriptions are excluded.

categories.name: Following search results
categories.content: Left click a result to go to and highlight it. Hold the right mouse button for a popup preview. Up/Down and Enter navigate too. Clear or Escape returns to browsing.

categories.name: Hotkey reference
categories.content: Hotkeys are grouped by where they work. Filter by context, mod or text.

categories.name: Window state
categories.content: Filters and the selected mod are preserved when resizing and reopening.

categories.name: Writing a mod document
categories.content: Use help.<lowercase mod folder>.name, hotkeys and categories. The compatibility root help.mods.<folder> is also accepted. The display name can differ from the actual folder key. Active mods without help categories or hotkeys are omitted from the mod list.

categories.name: Hotkey JSON example
categories.content: The preferred hotkey record contains keys, name, description and type. Example: { "keys": "Ctrl+F", "name": "Search help", "description": "Show the help search panel", "type": "EVERYWHERE" }. The records can be a JSON array or an object with numeric keys.

categories.name: Context aliases
categories.content: EVERYWHERE, GLOBAL, ANY and ALL mean a global binding. MAIN_MENU is supported explicitly. ADV_MAP, HERO, TOWN, COMBAT and OTHER select their respective contexts. Legacy numeric values -1 through 6 are supported; missing or unknown types go to Other.

categories.name: Legacy JSON compatibility
categories.content: The old categories.hotkeys.content format remains accepted with key or keys fields and numeric context values. The preferred format takes precedence when it yields records. Missing optional names/descriptions do not expose unresolved language keys.

categories.name: Category JSON example
categories.content: A category is { "name": "Rules", "content": "The rules of this mod...", "objects": [] }. Numeric category and hotkey objects may have short gaps; parsing stops after 32 consecutive missing records. Arrays should normally use consecutive indices.

categories.name: Text object example
categories.content: Text objects without overlay are appended to the category's scrollable document. Overlay text uses x, y, width and height within the content panel. zOrder determines the order of positioned objects. See the interactive examples below.

categories.name: Image object example
categories.content: Image objects accept an existing game PCX or DEF resource. DEF records use frame. The image must fit within the requested rectangle. Missing or oversized resources are skipped; their text documentation remains available.

categories.name: Navigation actions
categories.content: Buttons and links accept creatures:<id>, artifacts:<id>, heroes:<id>, spells:<id>, skills:<id>, towns:<id>, mod:<folder>:<category>, search and guide. Mod category indices include the hotkey category when one is present. IDs refer to the current game's native tables.

categories.name: Web links
categories.content: A Link record may use a full http:// or https:// URL. It is opened only when the user clicks the link. Link labels should describe the destination; the help reader does not follow URLs during parsing or search.

categories.name: ERM actions
categories.content: An ErmFunction record names an existing ERM function or its positive numeric ID. Clicking it executes a no-argument function call. Merely opening a category never executes ERM. The example record refers to a demonstration function that mod authors can implement.

categories.name: Integration API
categories.content: ERAHelp_ShowDialog(page, subtype) opens a page/category. ERAHelp_ShowObject(page, id) navigates to a particular game object. Calls must occur on the game's UI thread. Stable export names and the decorated stdcall names are available.

categories.name: Data and supported limits
categories.content: The native tables supply 163 heroes, 28 secondary skills, nine towns and 81 spells, including creature abilities. Creature and artifact counts come from the game. Additional scripted towns, skills or spells require their own metadata/API support and are not inferred from unrelated memory.

categories.name: Interactive navigation example
categories.content: These buttons demonstrate navigation to native objects and built-in help tools.

categories.name: Images and overlay example
categories.content: This category combines a game sprite, positioned explanation and a link.

objects.value: Creature portraits use a frame offset of two in TwCrPort.def.
An artifact image is a DEF frame; its native ID is also the frame index.
This non-overlay text is appended to the scrollable document.

categories.name: Web link example
categories.content: This sample opens the author's public source repository only when clicked.

categories.name: ERM function example
categories.content: Install examples/HelpDialogExample.erm in an active mod's Data/s directory and restart the game. The button below then calls the supplied demonstration function to show a message. Opening this category never invokes it.

categories.name: Mod category navigation example
categories.content: Internal mod links identify a lower-case folder key and a category index. The hotkey page, if present, occupies category zero.

categories.name: Plugin descriptions
categories.content:
Active physical mods with matching files get a Plugins section. Mods without their own help content or matching files are omitted. It scans EraPlugins, EraPlugins/BeforeWog and EraPlugins/AfterWog for .era, .dll and .bin files. Backup files and other subfolders are ignored. This lists supplied files, including dependencies; it does not report load status. Optional plugin notes use help.<mod-folder>.plugins, matched by relative file path or filename. Full paths take precedence.

Example:
"plugins": [
  { "file": "EraPlugins/MyPlugin.era", "name": "My plugin", "description": "Adds a feature." },
  { "file": "EraPlugins/AfterWog/Fix.bin", "description": "Applies a patch after WoG." }
]

A top-level description creates an Overview section. These generated sections are appended, preserving existing category indices.

guide.content:
Browse
Choose a tab. Objects are sorted by ID. Left click an object for details; hold right click for a preview.

Filters
Categories are on the left; other filters are above the objects. Left click: next value. Right click: previous value. Reset clears filters.

Search
Type a title in the top Search field. Ctrl+F focuses it. Left click a result to go to and highlight it. Hold right click for a preview. Up/Down and Enter navigate too. Clear or Escape returns to browsing.

Hotkeys
Bindings are grouped by where they work.

0.description: Castle combines human troops and angels. Its creature roster and default hero classes are listed above.

1.description: Rampart combines forest creatures and elven troops. Check the live roster and individual creature cards for the current mod's values.

2.description: Tower combines magical troops and constructs. Its hero and creature details are supplied by the current game tables.

3.description: Inferno combines demonic troops. Optional WoG scripts may change its special mechanics; consult the mod documentation for those rules.

4.description: Necropolis combines undead troops. Use the undead filter to compare creatures across factions and the Necromancy skill card to inspect its current descriptions.

5.description: Dungeon combines subterranean creatures and dragons. Use school and creature filters to compare the available magic and troops.

7.description: Fortress combines swamp troops. Creature cards show defense, health, speed, costs and documented traits.

8.description: Conflux combines elemental troops. Multi-school spells can appear in more than one school category.

heroes iii.description: Standard game controls, grouped by screen. Mods may override individual bindings. Spellbook, creature and System Options commands apply inside their respective windows.

categories.name: Keyboard reference
categories.content: Standard controls shared with Heroes III. The publisher manual lists them on pages 18-19. Its HD Edition graphics-switch command is not a feature of this ERA installation.

hd mod.name: HD mod
hd mod.description: Shown when HD mod is loaded. Controls depend on HD version, enabled UI tweaks and ERA compatibility. Army management applies to troop slots in adventure, hero, meeting, town and garrison panels. A hero keeps at least one creature. Costume slots are shared by the player; missing artifacts are skipped. Other bindings show their window in the title.

hotkeys.name: Reorder hero / town
hotkeys.description: Click its list portrait to move it first.

categories.name: HD controls and compatibility
categories.content: LMB: left mouse button. MMB: middle mouse button. Modified army clicks apply to creature slots; modified artifact clicks apply to artifact slots. For the original split dialog, select a stack before holding Shift. ERA does not support every HD feature. GEM can override artifact clicks, loading and battle actions.
